title: Sylvan Systems listing onramp & ops lab

Provision sandbox VPC and share peering details
Schedule 3-hour lab for KMS and SSO integration (tentative next Tue)
Run 48-hour smoke perf pilot with 10M tokens/day profile
action_items: Alex Chen: Share listing checklist + sample listing YAML (due: 2026-06-12)
Priya Rao: Prep quantization/perf workbook and dataset (due: 2026-06-15)
Omar Khan: Provide SSO/SAML metadata and test account (due: 2026-06-14)

summary: Partner onboarding sync to validate Sylvan Systems marketplace listing requirements, network/KMS/SAML gating, and plan a hands-on lab for private deployment on Redwood Private. Agreed to sandbox, checklist delivery, and a perf pilot. Some talk about quantization tradeoffs and KV cache behavior on long-context workloads.
transcript:
Header: 2026-06-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 62 mins | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Rao, Marco Valdez (Redwood) — Dana Liu, Omar Khan, Evelyn Park, Luis Moreno (Sylvan)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh quick roll call — alex here, priya and marco with me.
[00:09] Dana Liu: hey, dana here. thanks for setting this up.
[00:12] Omar Khan: omar — platform eng.
[00:15] Evelyn Park: evelyn, security.
[00:17] Luis Moreno: luis, devops.
[00:19] Alex Chen: awesome. today we want to go through the marketplace listing onramp items, make sure networking/KMS/SSO lines up, and propose an ops lab to validate the private deployment path. we'll call out blockers and assign owners. sound good?
[00:31] Dana Liu: yep, that's the goal. we have a Q2 timeline to list in the marketplace — need the checklist and a sandbox to test.
[00:37] Priya Rao: perfect. i'll start with a quick overview of the checklist and the pieces we usually require, then marco will go into networking and perf considerations.
[00:45] Marco Valdez: sounds good. heads up — i'm going to talk a bit about quantization tradeoffs because sylvan's inference profile is long context and that changes how batching/kv caching behaves.
[00:56] Omar Khan: yeah, we have 16k tokens contexts frequently, so curious what you mean by kv cash — k-v cash? i think our notes said kv cache.
[01:04] Marco Valdez: yeah sorry, kv cache — the key-value cache. in some quantized runtimes we see slower cold-starts on long-context because the cache fill patterns differ, and that affects latency percentiles.
[01:16] Evelyn Park: is that a security surface? like, does kv caching change encryption or data residency?
[01:21] Priya Rao: good question—no, cache is in-memory and cleared per session; data-at-rest policies still rely on KMS and disk encryption. but for Private we can ensure KV never spills to disk, or that spilled pages are encrypted with the customer's KMS.
[01:34] Luis Moreno: okay, we need that KMS guarantee. our compliance requires customer-owned keys for anything that could be persisted.
[01:40] Alex Chen: that's in our standard private deployment playbook; we support bring-your-own-KMS with HSM-backed keys. we'll capture the architecture doc.
[01:46] Dana Liu: can you share the exact diagram? our compliance team will need it for vendor review.
[01:51] Marco Valdez: yes — i'll drop the KMS flow and where encryption happens. quick caveat: when you use aggressive quantization (4-bit) there are some model compatibility checks, we usually run a tiny lab to validate generation quality.
[02:04] Omar Khan: that's fine. what's the expected impact on latency and throughput?
[02:08] Priya Rao: typically you see 1.5–2x throughput improvement but sometimes a 5–15% quality delta on certain prompts. for long sequences you might see less throughput gain because of kv cache behavior.
[02:19] Dana Liu: we need metrics. a simple matrix: 8-bit baseline, 4-bit fast path, with cost per million tokens and 95th latency.
[02:27] Alex Chen: absolutely — priya will prepare a perf workbook with those columns and some suggested test prompts.
[02:33] Marco Valdez: now on networking — for a marketplace listing we need a sandbox VPC peering and a NAT egress plan. ideally sylvan will provision a test VPC and we will peer for the lab. internal note: preserve routing to KMS endpoint through the peering.
[02:47] Omar Khan: we do have a staging VPC we can use. how does peering work with your private control plane?
[02:53] Alex Chen: for Redwood Private we run the control plane as a customer-managed component; the runtime sits in your VPC. peering connects control-plane APIs to runtime management endpoints. we'll provide a small terraform module to wire it up.
[03:04] Luis Moreno: terraform — yes please. we prefer IaC.
[03:07] Marco Valdez: noted. also, if you want faster ingress for model artifacts, we can support a restricted S3 role and signed URLs — we'll include that in the module.
[03:16] Evelyn Park: on SSO — we need SAML metadata and a test SP/IdP to validate attribute mapping to RBAC roles. what does redwood expect for role claims?
[03:26] Priya Rao: we accept SAML or OIDC. role mapping is flexible — we'd like an attribute called 'redwood_role' or we can map groups to RBAC labels. typical fields: email, groups, and an optional role attribute.
[03:37] Omar Khan: i'll export the SAML metadata and a test user.
[03:40] Dana Liu: one of our compliance guys will test SAML binding types — do you support HTTP-POST and Redirect?
[03:46] Alex Chen: yes both, plus OIDC. we'll send our SP metadata.
[03:50] Marco Valdez: quick note about audit logs — for marketplace listing we need to demonstrate audit retention. Redwood can ship per-route logs into your SIEM via secure forwarder, or drop into a customer-owned S3 bucket encrypted with your KMS.
[04:03] Evelyn Park: we prefer customer-owned S3 with SSE-KMS. can you confirm logs include token-level cost attribution or just request metadata?
[04:11] Alex Chen: token-level attribution is available in the Console as metadata, we can export per-request token counts as part of the log record. sampling option available if retention cost is a concern.
[04:22] Luis Moreno: sampling is fine for early testing.
[04:25] Marco Valdez: moving on to listing assets — we need a support email, logo, short description, security pdf (SOC2), and brief deployment guide. also contact for billing.
[04:36] Dana Liu: we have a vendor pack, but we need the exact template.
[04:39] Alex Chen: i'll send the template after this call. action: alex to share listing checklist and template.
[04:44] Omar Khan: for the perf pilot — what's the recommended load? we want it to mimic production but keep it contained.
[04:50] Priya Rao: recommended is 10M tokens/day over 48 hours with traffic skew: 70% short chat, 30% long-context completions. that should surface latency p95 and memory patterns.
[05:02] Dana Liu: ok we'll allocate that. can you provide a client script or harness?
[05:06] Marco Valdez: yes, we'll give a stress harness and a prompt corpus.
[05:10] Evelyn Park: security review — do you conduct pen-tests on the runtime?
[05:14] Alex Chen: Redwood runs internal pen tests and we provide a pen-test summary for marketplace reviews. for Private, customers can run their own with a scoped engagement and a test window.
[05:24] Evelyn Park: good. we'll plan an external penetration test after the lab.
[05:28] Luis Moreno: anything about data retention for the sandbox? logs only? model prompts?
[05:32] Priya Rao: sandbox will not persist prompts to disk; request logs retained as configured to your S3; snapshots of model artifacts only if you opt-in.
[05:40] Omar Khan: one more thing — license for the runtime components? open-source bits and a bundled license?
[05:45] Alex Chen: runtime uses a mix — some open-source libraries and Redwood-licensed orchestration. legal will send standard listing terms.
[05:52] Dana Liu: let's talk timeline — our marketplace listing gate is end of Q3, but initial listing in staging by end of next month would be great.
[06:00] Alex Chen: timeline looks feasible. proposed schedule: 1) today send checklist & terraform module, 2) sylvan provisions sandbox VPC this week, 3) we run a 3-hour hands-on lab next Tue to wire SAML/KMS, 4) perf pilot 48-hour after lab.
[06:15] Dana Liu: that works. i'll coordinate internal stakeholders.
[06:18] Marco Valdez: i'll also include a short checklist for quantization and model compatibility tests so you know what prompts to expect quality regressions on.
[06:26] Luis Moreno: can we get estimated cost for the pilot? even a ballpark so finance knows.
[06:31] Alex Chen: yes — priya we'll give a cost sheet, per-token estimate for hosted vs private.
[06:35] Priya Rao: i'll include both, and show the effect of batching and quantization on unit cost.
[06:40] Omar Khan: do you support canary rollouts for model versions in private? we want a safe way to test a new quantized build.
[06:46] Marco Valdez: yes — we support routing policies and rollback. for private we provide the same semantics via a local config and control-plane flags.
[06:53] Evelyn Park: last question — network egress IPs for allowlisting?
[06:57] Alex Chen: for private the runtime is in your VPC so egress is your control; for hosted you'd get a fixed egress range. we'll give the CIDR ranges if needed.
[07:06] Dana Liu: okay that's it from me. thanks.
[07:08] Alex Chen: great — to recap: alex sends checklist and marketplace template; priya sends perf workbook and cost sheet; marco sends KMS/quantization diagrams and terraform module; omar provides SAML metadata and provisions sandbox VPC; evelyn provides SOC2 scope and KMS diagram; we schedule a 3-hour lab next Tue (tentative).
[07:27] Dana Liu: i'll confirm times and invite the rest of the team.
[07:30] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc links and ticket numbers.

Notes: occasional transcription artefacts: "K-V cash" instead of KV cache, "V-P-C" said as letters. Some speaker labels corrected post-call.

End of recording.
